newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end rollercoaster day almost unmoved.
newsitem.headline: German shares end rollercoaster day almost unmoved.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index ended share trade on Tuesday almost unchanged from its opening level, having peaked and troughed like a rollercoaster over the course of a jittery day's trade.
The IBIS DAX index, which gauges electronic trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, ended just above the psychologically-key 3,000-point level at 3,000.66 points, up 1.47 points or 0.05 percent.

Earlier its floor trade counterpart, the DAX index, ended down 53.97 points, or 1.78 percent, at 2,976.71 points. Dealers said market nervousness at recent record levels on the index was finally translating into a long-anticipated correction.

"We started off brightly but no-one really knew why. There is a lot of nervousness about and there has been for a while, and you wouldn't want to get carried away with optimism on a day like this," said one trader.

As the day wore on, market-players became nervous in advance of comments by the U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, but in the end the market rose as his comments did not seem to indicate the possibility of interest rate hikes in the U.S.
A strong performer over the day was Germany's biggest bank, Deutsche Bank AG, which ended the day up 1.93 marks at 82.27 marks.
One of its rivals, Commerzbank AG, came off earlier losses and ended the day down 59 pfennigs at 44.35 marks.
Shares in chemicals and metals group Degussa AG ended up 28.80 marks at 744.85 marks after the group said pre-tax profits jumped 20 percent in the first quarter of the 1996/97 business year.

Another big gainer was the drugs and chemicals group Merck KGaA, which ended electronic trade up 2.35 marks at 60.40 marks after reporting an 11.3 percent rise in 1996 group sales and forecasting a strong profit growth for the year.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG shares also ended IBIS trade higher, up 60 pfennigs at 22.88 marks, as dealers said the stock broke through a point of technical resistance.

Such resistance points occur for financial securities because of the balance of demand and supply in the market. Once a security has breached a resistance point, it can often go on to make large gains.
